Data Analysis: immune response

Immunity * sex interaction

Total_wbc: the total count of white blood cells circulating in the blood stream

# Prepare variables
data$treatment <- factor(data$treatment,
                       levels = c("control", "low", "high"))

data$sex <- factor(data$sex)
data$tank_id <- factor(data$tank_id)
data$body_mass_sc <- scale(data$body_mass)

# Total WBC interaction model
m1_wbc_int <- glmmTMB(
  total_wbc ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_wbc_int)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          total_wbc ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1039.0   1065.3   -510.5   1021.0      128 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance  Std.Dev.
##  tank_id (Intercept) 9.184e-10 3.03e-05
## Number of obs: 137, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.0991 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)            3.46224    0.06936   49.92   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow          -0.06182    0.09239   -0.67   0.5034    
## treatmenthigh          0.11657    0.09969    1.17   0.2423    
## sexmale                0.11570    0.09592    1.21   0.2278    
## body_mass_sc          -0.03002    0.02709   -1.11   0.2678    
## treatmentlow:sexmale   0.01652    0.13185    0.13   0.9003    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.23524    0.13400   -1.76   0.0792 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
res_wbc_int <- simulateResiduals(m1_wbc_int)
plot(res_wbc_int)

testDispersion(res_wbc_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0415, p-value = 0.712
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_wbc_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_wbc_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 1, observations = 137, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.0001847844 0.0399968207
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.00729927
Anova(m1_wbc_int, type = "III")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: total_wbc
##                   Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
## (Intercept)   2492.0276  1     <2e-16 ***
## treatment        3.5513  2     0.1694    
## sex              1.4548  1     0.2278    
## body_mass_sc     1.2281  1     0.2678    
## treatment:sex    4.4222  2     0.1096    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(
  m1_wbc_int,
  pairwise ~ treatment | sex,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)
## $emmeans
## sex = female:
##  treatment response   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  control       31.9 2.21 Inf      27.8      36.5
##  low           30.0 1.86 Inf      26.5      33.9
##  high          35.8 2.60 Inf      31.1      41.3
## 
## sex = male:
##  treatment response   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  control       35.8 2.32 Inf      31.5      40.6
##  low           34.2 2.39 Inf      29.8      39.2
##  high          31.8 1.96 Inf      28.2      35.9
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## 
## $contrasts
## sex = female:
##  contrast       ratio     SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.064 0.0983 Inf    1   0.669  0.7815
##  control / high 0.890 0.0887 Inf    1  -1.169  0.4716
##  low / high     0.837 0.0795 Inf    1  -1.877  0.1452
## 
## sex = male:
##  contrast       ratio     SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.046 0.0985 Inf    1   0.481  0.8803
##  control / high 1.126 0.1010 Inf    1   1.327  0.3798
##  low / high     1.076 0.1000 Inf    1   0.788  0.7102
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
emmeans(
  m1_wbc_int,
  pairwise ~ sex | treatment,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)

Plotting: WBC x sex

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare labels
#---------------------------------------------------------

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Colour palettes for sex
# Same as previous sex-split behavioural plots
#---------------------------------------------------------

sex_pastel_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#D8B4E2",
  "Male"   = "#A9CCE3"
)


sex_dark_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#8E44AD",
  "Male"   = "#2874A6"
)

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

pj <- position_jitterdodge(
  jitter.width = 0.12,
  dodge.width = 0.75
)

#=========================================================
# 1) TOTAL WBC
#=========================================================

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Estimated marginal means
#---------------------------------------------------------

emm_wbc_int_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(
    m1_wbc_int,
    ~ sex | treatment,
    type = "response"
  )
)

cn <- names(emm_wbc_int_df)

mean_col <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])

lower_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)]
)

upper_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)]
)

emm_wbc_int_df <- emm_wbc_int_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Plot total WBC
#---------------------------------------------------------

p_wbc_sex <- ggplot() +

  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = total_wbc,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = interaction(treatment_plot, sex_plot)
    ),
    position = pd,
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = NA,
    linewidth = 0
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = total_wbc,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pj,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_wbc_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_wbc_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Total white blood cells",
    fill = "Sex",
    colour = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_wbc_sex)

Main effects model

m1_wbc <- glmmTMB(
  total_wbc ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_wbc)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          total_wbc ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1039.4   1059.8   -512.7   1025.4      130 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance  Std.Dev. 
##  tank_id (Intercept) 5.261e-09 7.253e-05
## Number of obs: 137, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.102 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)    3.50240    0.05707   61.37   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow  -0.06084    0.06691   -0.91    0.363    
## treatmenthigh -0.01295    0.06747   -0.19    0.848    
## sexmale        0.04143    0.05731    0.72    0.470    
## body_mass_sc  -0.02507    0.02738   -0.92    0.360    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(m1_wbc)
plot(simulationOutput)

testDispersion(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0463, p-value = 0.68
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(simulationOutput)

##

Immunity * sex interaction

N.L_ratio: neutrophil-to-lymphocye ratio. Two of the most abundant white blood cells.

# N:L ratio interaction model
m1_nl_int <- glmmTMB(
  n.l_ratio ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_nl_int)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          n.l_ratio ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   -238.6   -212.3    128.3   -256.6      128 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  tank_id (Intercept) 0.03004  0.1733  
## Number of obs: 137, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.265 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)           -1.492229   0.129964 -11.482   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow          -0.121038   0.178041  -0.680    0.497    
## treatmenthigh         -0.306842   0.187718  -1.635    0.102    
## sexmale               -0.012387   0.158418  -0.078    0.938    
## body_mass_sc           0.006876   0.047724   0.144    0.885    
## treatmentlow:sexmale   0.006107   0.224633   0.027    0.978    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.014043   0.225747  -0.062    0.950    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
res_nl_int <- simulateResiduals(m1_nl_int)
plot(res_nl_int)

testDispersion(res_nl_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0877, p-value = 0.584
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_nl_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_nl_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 2, observations = 137, p-value = 0.298
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.001772866 0.051738898
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.01459854
Anova(m1_nl_int, type = "III")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: n.l_ratio
##                  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
## (Intercept)   131.8330  1     <2e-16 ***
## treatment       2.6987  2     0.2594    
## sex             0.0061  1     0.9377    
## body_mass_sc    0.0208  1     0.8854    
## treatment:sex   0.0081  2     0.9960    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(
  m1_nl_int,
  pairwise ~ treatment | sex,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)

emmeans(

Main effects model

# 1) Prepare variables
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high")
    ),
    sex = factor(sex),
    tank_id = factor(tank_id),
    body_mass_sc = as.numeric(scale(body_mass)),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    )
  )


# 2) Model: Gamma GLMM

m1_nl <- glmmTMB(
  n.l_ratio ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_nl)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          n.l_ratio ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   -242.6   -222.2    128.3   -256.6      130 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  tank_id (Intercept) 0.03006  0.1734  
## Number of obs: 137, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.265 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)   -1.490761   0.111248 -13.400   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow  -0.118564   0.139850  -0.848    0.397    
## treatmenthigh -0.314662   0.140396  -2.241    0.025 *  
## sexmale       -0.015149   0.096360  -0.157    0.875    
## body_mass_sc   0.007332   0.047387   0.155    0.877    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# 3) Diagnostics

res_nl <- simulateResiduals(m1_nl)
plot(res_nl)

testDispersion(res_nl)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0876, p-value = 0.584
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_nl)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_nl
## outliers at both margin(s) = 2, observations = 137, p-value = 0.298
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.001772866 0.051738898
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.01459854
# 4) Type II ANOVA
Anova(m1_nl, type = "II")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: n.l_ratio
##               Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)  
## treatment    5.1098  2     0.0777 .
## sex          0.0247  1     0.8751  
## body_mass_sc 0.0239  1     0.8770  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
anova(m1_nl, m1_nl_int)
## Data: data
## Models:
## m1_nl: n.l_ratio ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id), zi=~0, disp=~1

## m1_nl_int  9 -238.61 -212.33  128.3  -256.61 0.0081      2      0.996
# 5) Estimated marginal means
emm_nl <- emmeans(

      x = treatment_plot,
      y = n.l_ratio,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.18,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_nl_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_nl_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = treatment_plot
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_nl)
